texts.preamble: Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer vs Sh.K.S.R. Kumar (Manager) on 24 February, 2018 In The Court Of Ms.Poonam A. Bamba:District & Sessions Judge: New Delhi Crl. Appeal No. 8441/17 Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer Department of Pfa Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20 Lawrence Road Indl. Area,New Delhi110035. Versus 1. Sh.K.S.R. Kumar (Manager) S/o Late Sh. Veerraju M/s Southern Super Market Pvt. Ltd. 18/2, Arya Samaj Road, Karol Bagh New Delhi110005. R/o 7052, Gali No.5 Mata Rameshwari Nehru Nagar Karol Bagh, New Delhi. 2. Sh. A. K. Mohan S/o Shri A. V. Rao M/s Southern Super Market Pvt. Ltd. 18/2, Arya Samaj Road, Karol Bagh New Delhi110005. 3. M/s Southern Super Market Pvt. Ltd. 18/2, Arya Samaj Road, Karol Bagh New Delhi110005. Appeal Under Sections 377 Code Of Criminal Procedure Against The Order Dated 28.09.2012 Of Ld.Acmmii, New Delhi. Date of Institution of Appeal : 03.01.2013 Arguments concluded on : 24.02.2018 Judgment announced on : 24.02.2018 Present : Sh. A.K. Mishra, Ld. Addl. Public Prosecutor for the State Sh. Anurag Ahluwalia, Ld. Counsel for the respondents J U D G M E N T
texts.arguments: Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that though the appellant has some prima facie case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about the sentence which has been imposed by the courts below. He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable. He has drawn our attention to the judgment of this Court in 'T. Barai v. Henry Ah Hoe and Another' [1983 (1) SCC 177] wherein this Court held that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused persons, it can be applied even with respect to earlier cases as well which are pending in the Court. In the said judgment, the Court held as under: "22. It is only retroactive criminal legislation that is prohibited under Article 20(1). The prohibition contained in Article 20(1) is that no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence prohibits nor shall he be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence. The rule of beneficial construction requires that even ex post facto law of such a type should be applied to mitigate the rigour of the law. This finds support in the following passage from Craies on Statute Law, 7th Edn., at pp. 38889: A retrospective statute is different from an ex post facto statute. "Every ex post facto law...." said Chase, J., in the American case of Calder v. Bull "must necessarily be retrospective, but every retrospective law is not an ex post facto law. Every law that takes away or impairs rights vested agreeably to existing laws is retrospective, and is generally unjust and may be oppressive; it is a good general rule that a law should have no retrospect, but in cases in which the laws may justly and for the benefit of the community and also of individuals relate to a time antecedent to their commencement: as statutes of oblivion or of pardon. But I do not consider any law ex post facto within the prohibition that mollifies the rigour of the criminal law, but only those that create or aggravate the crime, or increase the punishment or change the rules of evidence for the purpose Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer vs Sh.K.S.R. Kumar (Manager) on 24 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183710211/ 6 of conviction.... 5.7 Hon'ble High Court Of Delhi in State V Amar Singh 2016 Cr.LJ 583, which involved mis branding upheld the punishment of TRC, i.e. less than the minimum prescribed under FSA Act, considering inter alia that the said offence is now punishable with fine only under the new Act i.e. FSSA.
